newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Statoil begins tests on Irish oil field.
newsitem.headline: Statoil begins tests on Irish oil field.

text.p: Norway's Statoil said on Friday its Irish unit Statoil Exploration (Ireland) Ltd had started a long-term production well test on its Connemara oil field off the west coast of Ireland.
The purpose of the test was to study reservoir and production characteristics in order to make a decision on whether to declare the field commercial, Statoil said.
"The decision is likely to be made in the autumn. If positive, full oil production would begin in 1998," the Norwegian state oil company said in a statement
This would be the first oil produced from a Statoil-developed and operated field outside Norway.
The Connemara field, discovered in 1979, is located off the west coast of Ireland in water depths of 370 metres.
